notes.message: Greenhouse documents that it cannot parse a resume larger than 2.5 MB: the file is only attached, and its details are left to be typed in by hand.
Greenhouse lists columns, tables, headers and footers, graphics, and a name or contact details in a header, footer or text box among the causes of a failed or partial parse.
Lever documents that it cannot parse a resume saved as an image (JPG, PNG), and suggests a test: if you cannot select the text in the file, it is likely not parseable.

In Oracle Taleo each employer's administrators choose which file formats candidates may attach, so use one the careers site offers; PDF, Word (.doc, .docx), RTF, HTML and plain text are among those Taleo supports.

default.message: The file name does not say whose resume it is, or reads as a draft. Recruiters see it in the ATS and in their downloads, beside everyone else's.

fileNameDraft.default: The file is named "{name}", which reads as a draft: {marks}.

default.message: The file is larger than {limit}. Many ATS upload forms and parsers stop at about that size; it is a common limit, not a universal one.
default.fix: Shrink or remove the images and export again; a resume of text alone is well under {limit}.

default.message: The file is password-protected or encrypted. An ATS that cannot open it reads nothing, and some refuse an encrypted file even when it opens without a password.
default.fix: Save a copy with no password or security settings, and upload that.

default.message: The document still holds tracked changes. A recruiter who opens it in Word sees the edits, and a parser may read deleted text as if it were there.
default.fix: In Word, accept or reject every change (Review, Accept All Changes), turn Track Changes off, and save again.

default.message: The document still holds comments. A recruiter who opens it in Word sees them.
default.fix: In Word, delete them (Review, Delete All Comments in Document) and save again.

default.message: A graduation year more than {years} years back lets a reader work out your age, which can invite age bias. Leaving off graduation years older than about 15 years is common advice; the degree and the school are what a screen checks.
default.fix: Keep the degree and the school, and leave the year off.

default.message: More than {years} years of experience, stated or dated in full, lets a reader work out your age, which can invite age bias.
default.fix: Show the last 15 years or so in detail, sum up earlier roles in a line without dates, and write "15+ years" rather than the full count.

experienceHistory.default: {n} years of work history are dated.
